notes: The Probate Division is at the Richard J. Daley Center, 50 West Washington St., Room 1202, Chicago. Phone 312-603-6441, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division)

There is no fee to file a will. You can file it in person at Room 1202, by mail to the Probate Division, or in person at any of the Clerk's 5 offices. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division)

The Probate Division's page says that to open an estate in Cook County you need to hire an attorney, who files the court forms through eFile Illinois. The filing cost is $479.00, with or without a will. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division)

After the court issues its order, the Clerk's Office issues Letters of Administration (no will) or Letters of Office (with a will). These are then taken to the Recorder of Deeds at 118 N. Clark Street. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division)

The Clerk of the Circuit Court has suburban district courthouses in Skokie, Rolling Meadows, Maywood, Bridgeview and Markham, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/suburban-districts-0)

The Clerk's suburban district lists place these towns as follows. District 2 (Skokie): Des Plaines, Evanston, Glenview, Northbrook, Skokie; District 3 (Rolling Meadows): Arlington Heights, Mount Prospect, Palatine, Schaumburg; District 4 (Maywood): Berwyn, Cicero, Oak Park; District 5 (Bridgeview): Oak Lawn, Orland Park, Tinley Park. These courthouses handle other case types; Cook County probate itself is heard at the Daley Center. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/suburban-districts-0)

Deeds and Transfer on Death Instruments are recorded at the Clerk's Recording Division, 118 N. Clark St., Room 120, Chicago. Documents cannot be recorded at courthouse satellite offices. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/agency/recordings)

E-recording goes through an approved submitter company. The page lists a flat $50 fee for e-filed Transfer on Death Instruments. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/recordings/how-to-mail-and-e-record-deeds)

The Clerk's Recordings Legal Help Desk offers free advice from legal aid attorneys on deed counseling and Transfer on Death Instruments on the third Thursday of each month at 118 N. Clark; call 312-603-5050. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/recordings/recordings-legal-help-desk)

The Assessor's senior exemption page says a property can stay eligible for a deceased parent who lived there on January 1, 2025, with a death certificate and letters of office or similar papers. A surviving spouse who is 65 or older qualifies in their own name. (source: https://www.cookcountyassessoril.gov/senior-citizen-exemption)
The Self-Represented Litigant Center is at the Daley Center, Room 602, phone 312-603-3530. The page describes no probate-specific help. (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/pro-se-slr)

clerk.name: Montgomery County Circuit Clerk
clerk.address: 120 North Main St, Room 125, Hillsboro, IL 62049

The County Clerk and Recorder is on the first floor of the Historic Courthouse at 1 Courthouse Square, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The recorder phone is (217) 532-9535. (source: https://www.montgomerycountyil.gov/county-clerk/)

counties.name: Morgan County
notes: The e-filing kiosk in the Morgan County Courthouse is in the basement. Listed hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/36/Morgan-County-Courthouse/court/)
The law library is on the 3rd floor, and the courthouse parking lot is free. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/36/Morgan-County-Courthouse/court/)

counties.name: Ogle County
notes: The Ogle County Circuit Clerk is in the Judicial Center, 106 S. 5th Street, Suite 300, Oregon. The Civil Division number is 815-732-1130 and hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.oglecountyil.gov/departments/circuit_clerk/contact_us.php)
The Circuit Clerk's site links to E-File guides, standards and exemptions. (source: https://www.oglecountyil.gov/departments/circuit_clerk/contact_us.php)
The Circuit Clerk posts a filing fee schedule dated 9-4-2026. Ask the clerk for the current probate fee before filing. (source: https://www.oglecountyil.gov/departments/circuit_clerk/filing_fees.php)

The County Clerk & Recorder at 105 S 5th St, Ste 104, Oregon indexes recorded property documents, and the original is returned to the person who presented it. Phone is (815) 732-1110. (source: https://www.oglecountyil.gov/departments/county_clerk/index.php)

counties.name: Peoria County

clerk.name: Peoria County Circuit Clerk
clerk.address: 324 Main Street, Room G-22, Peoria, IL 61602

notes: Peoria County is in the 10th Judicial Circuit, together with Marshall, Putnam, Stark and Tazewell counties. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/38/Peoria-County-Court-Administration/court/)

The Self-Help Center and the law library are in Room 211 of the courthouse. Four public computers there can be used for free legal research and for e-filing with the Circuit Clerk. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/38/Peoria-County-Court-Administration/court/)

The Peoria County Circuit Clerk's filing fee list, titled 9/4/26, shows a $281.00 filing fee for Administration of Decedent's Estate. The document does not state a separate effective date. (source: https://www.peoriacounty.gov/DocumentCenter/View/18900/Peoria-County-Circuit-Clerk-Filing-Fees-9426)
In Peoria County, recording is handled under the County Clerk at 309-672-6090. The county directory lists no separate Recorder of Deeds. (source: https://www.peoriacounty.gov/directory)

Peoria County offers a $5,000 Senior Homestead Exemption at age 65, a Senior Assessment Freeze with a $65,000 income limit, and a Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program. Call the Supervisor of Assessments at 309-672-6910. (source: https://www.peoriacounty.gov/399/Tax-Relief-Exemptions)

counties.name: Perry County
notes: The Perry County Circuit Clerk is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the page links to statewide eFile. (source: https://perrycountyil.gov/perry-county-circuit-clerk/)
The Circuit Clerk's page lists 618-357-6726 as the phone number and circuitclerk@perrycountyil.gov as the email. (source: https://perrycountyil.gov/perry-county-circuit-clerk/)

counties.name: Piatt County
notes: Public access terminals with internet and printing are in the Circuit Clerk's Office on the 2nd floor and in the Law Library on the 3rd floor. The courthouse is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/39/Piatt-County-Courthouse/court/)

An e-filing kiosk with shortcuts and instructions for e-filers is in the public access terminal area, and the page links to statewide eFile. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/39/Piatt-County-Courthouse/court/)

counties.name: Pike County
notes: The Pike County Courthouse, 100 E. Washington Street, Pittsfield, is listed by the Illinois Courts directory as open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/105/Pike-County-Courthouse/court/)
An e-filing kiosk is located in the foyer of the Pike County Circuit Clerk's office. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/105/Pike-County-Courthouse/court/)

counties.name: Pope County
notes: The Pope County Circuit Clerk's office is in the courthouse at 310 East Main Street, Golconda (mailing address P.O. Box 438). (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/circuit-courts/pope-county/)

The First Judicial Circuit states that its circuit clerk offices are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and that some close at noon, so call ahead before driving to Golconda. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/frequently-asked-questions)

counties.name: Pulaski County
notes: The Pulaski County Circuit Clerk's office is in the courthouse at 500 Illinois Avenue, Mound City. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/circuit-courts/pulaski-county/)

The First Judicial Circuit states that its circuit clerk offices are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and that some close at noon, so call ahead before visiting Mound City. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/frequently-asked-questions)

counties.name: Putnam County
notes: The Putnam County Circuit Clerk's office is in the courthouse at 120 N. 4th Street, Hennepin, and is open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, excluding holidays. (source: https://putnamil.gov/government/circuit_court_clerk_office/index.php)

The Putnam County Circuit Clerk's page states that civil filings must be made electronically, a requirement in effect since January 1, 2018. (source: https://putnamil.gov/government/circuit_court_clerk_office/index.php)

counties.name: Randolph County
notes: The Randolph County Self-Help Center is in the conference room on the 3rd floor of the courthouse, which is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The page also links to eFileIL. (source: https://illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/42/Randolph-County-Courthouse/court)

The Randolph County Clerk and Recorder is in Room 202 at 1 Taylor Street, phone (618) 826-5000 ext. 191, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The page lists sections for land records and recording fees. (source: https://randolphcountyil.gov/county-clerk-recorder/)

counties.name: Richland County
notes: The Richland County Courthouse, 103 W. Main Street, Olney, is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the Circuit Clerk is listed at Suite 21. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/106/Richland-County-Courthouse/court/)
The courthouse has an e-filing kiosk with computers and scanners for filing through eFileIL. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/106/Richland-County-Courthouse/court/)

counties.name: Rock Island County
notes: Probate walk-in is held every day from 9:00 to 9:30 a.m. in Courtroom 402. It covers matters such as uncontested opening and closing of estates and petitions to sell real estate. (source: https://rockislandcountyil.gov/787/Rock-Island-County-Probate)
The county's probate page offers forms for a Petition for Probate and for Letters, a Small Estate Affidavit and an Inventory. (source: https://rockislandcountyil.gov/787/Rock-Island-County-Probate)

The Recorder's Office is at 1504 3rd Avenue, 2nd Floor, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It records deeds, mortgages, releases and liens. (source: https://rockislandcountyil.gov/308/Recorders-Office)
The recording fee schedule effective February 1, 2025 lists $83 for a conforming document and $104 for a non-conforming document. (source: https://rockislandcountyil.gov/314/Fees)

The county courthouse at 1317 3rd Avenue is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The state courts directory lists a self-help center and a law library there. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/142/Rock-Island-County-Courthouse/court/)

counties.name: Saline County
notes: The Saline County page of the First Judicial Circuit lists Mary Kuczynski as Circuit Clerk at the Saline County Courthouse, 10 East Poplar, Harrisburg, phone 618-253-5096, and links to the statewide eFile site. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/circuit-courts/saline-county/)
The same page links to Illinois Legal Self-Help Centers resources and lists Saline County Probation at 10 East Poplar Street. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/circuit-courts/saline-county/)

counties.name: Sangamon County
notes: Probate cases are filed with the Circuit Clerk in Room 405 on the 4th floor of the Sangamon County Courthouse, 200 South 9th Street, Springfield. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/43/Sangamon-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Sangamon County Self-Help Center is located in the Circuit Clerk's Office. An online law library terminal is on the 6th floor of the courthouse. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/43/Sangamon-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Circuit Clerk's office uses the statewide Electronic Filing Manager and has an e-filing kiosk in Room 405. The clerk advises allowing 30 to 45 minutes at the front counter to e-file. (source: https://www.sangamoncountycircuitclerk.org)

The Sangamon County fee schedule, marked updated 09/21/2026, lists a filing fee of $276.00 for Administration of Decedent's Estate. (source: https://www.sangamoncountycircuitclerk.org/application/files/8717/8973/7703/9-21-2026_Filing_Fees_Final.pdf)

The Sangamon County Recorder is a separate office from the County Clerk. Its page links to fee, e-recording and land records search information. (source: https://sangamonil.gov/departments/m-r/recorder)

The Sangamon County Treasurer runs a Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral program, and the Supervisor of Assessments handles homestead exemption applications. (source: https://sangamonil.gov/departments/s-z/supervisor-of-assessments/homestead-exemption)

counties.name: Shelby County
notes: The courthouse is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Mail goes to P.O. Box 469, Shelbyville, IL 62565, and the listed phone numbers are 217-774-4212 and 217-774-4109. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/45/Shelby-County-Courthouse/court)
An e-filing kiosk is on the third floor of the courthouse, and the page links to an eFileIL portal. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/45/Shelby-County-Courthouse/court)

counties.name: St. Clair County

probateCourt.name: St. Clair County Courthouse (Circuit Court, 20th Judicial Circuit)

recorder.name: St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds

notes: St. Clair County is in the 20th Judicial Circuit. The courthouse is at 10 Public Square, Belleville. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/109/St-Clair-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Circuit Clerk requires civil filings, including probate, to be e-filed through Odyssey eFileIL under Supreme Court Rule 9. The clerk's office has public e-filing computers for use during business hours. (source: https://www.stclaircountyil.gov/departments/circuit-clerk/efile)

The St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds is at 10 Public Square, Belleville. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Items received after 3:00 p.m. are recorded the next business day. Phone (618) 825-2481. (source: https://www.stclaircountyil.gov/Departments/RecorderofDeeds)

The Recorder's posted fee for recording a deed is $55.00 with the RHSP surcharge, plus transfer tax when it applies. Call the office about a specific document. (source: https://www.stclaircountyil.gov/Departments/RecorderofDeeds)

A Legal Self-Help Center is inside the Law Library at the St. Clair County Courthouse. It has six stations with internet access, printers and a copier. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/109/St-Clair-County-Courthouse/court/)

The St. Clair County Office on Aging is at 201 North Church Street, Belleville. Phone (618) 234-4410. It runs senior activities, caregiver workshops and a Senior Wellness Center. (source: https://www.stclaircountyil.gov/departments/office-on-aging)

counties.name: Stark County
notes: The Stark County Circuit Clerk's office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://starkco.illinois.gov/departments/circuit-clerk)

The Illinois Courts directory gives the Stark County Circuit Clerk's address as 130 West Main Street, Toulon, with mail going to P.O. Box 426. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/46/Stark-County-Courthouse/court/)

notes: The Circuit Clerk is on the 2nd floor of the courthouse at 15 N. Galena Ave., open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Press 3 for the Civil Division. (source: https://stephensoncountyil.gov/government/circuit_clerk_and_court/index.php)

The courthouse has a Self-Help Center and an e-filing kiosk on the 2nd floor next to the Circuit Clerk. The law library is also on the 2nd floor. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/47/Stephenson-County-Courthouse/court/)

The County Clerk and Recorder is at 50 West Douglas, Suite 500, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Documents recorded after July 1992 can be searched through the online Tapestry system. (source: https://stephensoncountyil.gov/government/county_clerk_and_recorder/index.php)

notes: The Tazewell County law library is in Room 103 on the first floor of the courthouse in Pekin. A paralegal is on staff and public computers are available. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/48/Tazewell-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Tazewell County Circuit Clerk posts a civil fee schedule titled Sept 10, 2026. Call the Circuit Clerk at 309-477-2214 to confirm the probate filing fee. (source: https://tazewellcountyil.com/fee-schedule/)

The County Clerk & Recorder is in the McKenzie Building, 11 S. 4th Street, Pekin. The Recorder's phone is 309-477-2210, and the page links to e-recording information. (source: https://tazewell-il.gov/countyclerkrecorder/)

The Tazewell County Assessment Office is at 11 South Fourth Street, Suite 410, Pekin, phone 309-477-2275. It handles Senior Homestead (Form 324) and Senior Freeze (Form 340) applications. (source: https://tazewell-il.gov/assessments/)

The First Judicial Circuit states that its circuit clerk offices are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and that some close at noon. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/frequently-asked-questions)

probateCourt.name: Rita B. Garman Vermilion County Courthouse

notes: An e-filing kiosk is on the first floor of the Circuit Clerk's office in the Rita B. Garman Vermilion County Courthouse. The court page also links to statewide eFileIL. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/49/Vermilion-County-Courthouse-Rita-B-Garman-Courthouse/court/)
Vermilion County is in the 5th Judicial Circuit, with Clark, Coles and Edgar counties. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/interactive-map)

The Vermilion County Recorder's standard document fee is $69.00 for deeds, mortgages and releases, effective July 1, 2023. The fee is $19.00 less if the grantor or grantee is a government entity. (source: https://www.vercounty.org/recorder/recording-fees/)

Call the Vermilion County Assessment Office at 217-554-1940 to have a Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption application mailed to you. (source: https://www.vercounty.org/supervisor-of-assessments/exemption-information/)

counties.name: Warren County
notes: The Warren County Circuit Clerk's office at 100 W. Broadway, Monmouth, is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.9thjudicial.org/locations/warren-county/6/location-details)
An e-filing computer station is set up on the 3rd floor of the Warren County Courthouse. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/51/Warren-County-Courthouse/court/)

recorder.name: Washington County Clerk & Recorder
recorder.address: 101 E. St. Louis Street, Nashville, IL 62263

notes: The Washington County Circuit Clerk's office is at 125 E. Elm Street, Nashville, open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (source: https://washingtonco.illinois.gov/circuit-clerk/)
The Circuit Clerk's court fee schedule lists a probate filing fee for testate and intestate estates of $371.00. (source: https://washingtonco.illinois.gov/circuit-clerk/court-fees/)

The County Clerk & Recorder works from a different building, 101 E. St. Louis Street, Nashville, so recording and court filings are at separate addresses. (source: https://washingtonco.illinois.gov/county-clerk/)

counties.name: Wayne County
notes: The Wayne County Circuit Clerk's office is in Suite 204 of the courthouse at 301 E. Main Street, Fairfield, and the courthouse is listed as open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/53/Wayne-County-Courthouse/court/)
The Wayne County Clerk is a separate office from the Circuit Clerk, with listed hours of Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (source: https://waynecountyil.gov/county-clerk/)

counties.name: White County
notes: The White County Circuit Clerk's office is in the courthouse at 301 E. Main Street, Carmi, and the Illinois Courts directory lists its hours as 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/54/White-County-Courthouse/court/)
The White County site says the Circuit Clerk maintains all Circuit Court records and collects all court-related fines and fees. (source: https://www.whitecounty-il.gov/circuit-clerk)

counties.name: Whiteside County

recorder.name: Whiteside County Recorder
recorder.address: 200 E Knox Street, Floor 2, Morrison, IL 61270

notes: The Probate Division is at 200 East Knox Street, Morrison, phone 815-772-5168. The Circuit Clerk also has a satellite office at 101 East Third Street, Sterling, phone 815-535-4530. (source: https://whitesidecountyil.gov/216/Circuit-Clerk)

The county fee schedule, revised October 1, 2025, lists $364.00 to file a decedent's estate. (source: https://whitesidecountyil.gov/DocumentCenter/View/201/Filling-Fees---Civil-Revised-April-2022-PDF)

The Recorder is at 200 E Knox Street, Floor 2, Morrison, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It accepts only originals or certified copies, and real estate documents must include tax parcel numbers. (source: https://www.whitesidecountyil.gov/285/Recorder---Land-Records)
Recorder fees listed are $79.00 for a standard document and $99.00 for an irregular document. (source: https://www.whitesidecountyil.gov/285/Recorder---Land-Records)

clerk.address: Will County Court House, 100 W. Jefferson Street, Joliet, IL 60432

notes: New estate cases in Will County must be filed electronically, not by mail. The clerk's site has a Small Estate Affidavit and a Decedent Estate Packet of forms. (source: https://www.circuitclerkofwillcounty.com/Civil/Probate)

The Self-Help Center is in the Law Library on the 3rd floor of the Will County Courthouse. E-filing kiosks are in the Law Library and in the Circuit Clerk's Office. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/110/Will-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Recorder of Deeds main office is at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. A Bolingbrook office at 241 Canterbury Lane is open Tuesday and Thursday. (source: https://willcountyrecorder.com/)

counties.name: Williamson County

probateCourt.name: Williamson County Courthouse (Circuit Court, 1st Judicial Circuit)

recorder.name: Williamson County Clerk and Recorder
recorder.address: 407 N. Monroe St, Suite 119, Marion, IL 62959

notes: Williamson County is in the 1st Judicial Circuit. The Circuit Clerk is at the courthouse, 200 W. Jefferson Street, Marion, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Phone 618-997-1301. (source: https://www.williamsoncountyil.gov/departments/circuit-clerk/)

The clerk's page lists a probate and guardianship line, extension 3447 on the main number. The page's own link shows extension 3439, so confirm when you call. (source: https://www.williamsoncountyil.gov/departments/circuit-clerk/)
The 1st Circuit's Williamson County page links to the statewide Illinois e-filing site. (source: https://firstcircuitil.org/circuit-courts/williamson-county/)
The courthouse listing includes a Self-Help Center link for self-represented litigants. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/148/Williamson-County-Courthouse/court/)

Deeds are recorded at the County Clerk and Recorder, 407 N. Monroe St, Suite 119, Marion. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Only original signed documents are accepted, and e-recording is available through approved partners. (source: https://www.williamsoncountyil.gov/records/land-records/)

A MyDec-generated PTAX form marked "Closing Completed" must accompany recorded documents in Williamson County. The office cannot give advice about transferring property. (source: https://www.williamsoncountyil.gov/records/land-records/)

counties.name: Winnebago County
notes: Wills are filed with the Circuit Clerk in Room 108 of the Winnebago County Courthouse. Bring the original will and any codicils, plus the date of birth and date of death. No fee is listed for filing the will itself. (source: https://www.circuitclerk.wincoil.gov/wills/)

The clerk's fee list effective July 20, 2026 shows $392.00 to open an Administration of Decedent's Estate case. Claims against an estate cost $25 to $60 depending on the amount. (source: https://www.circuitclerk.wincoil.gov/assets/1/7/Civil_Filing_Fee_List_-_07202026_V1.pdf)

Probate forms must be e-filed through an approved e-filing service provider. Wills cannot be filed electronically. The clerk's office cannot help prepare documents or give legal advice. (source: https://www.circuitclerk.wincoil.gov/civil-information/probate/probate/)

The Winnebago County Law Library is on the third floor of the courthouse at 400 W State St. It is open to the public during regular courthouse hours and has two public Westlaw terminals. (source: https://17thcircuit.illinoiscourts.gov/public-info/court-resources/law-library)

The Recorder's fee schedule effective January 1, 2025 lists $54.00 for a standard-format deed and $66.00 for a non-standard deed. (source: https://wincoil.gov/images/departments/recorder/forms/Predictable%20Fee%20Schedule%202025.pdf)

The Supervisor of Assessments is at 404 Elm St., Room 301, Rockford, phone (815) 319-4460. The senior citizen homestead exemption is for owners 65 or older who live in the home, and it reduces taxable value by up to $5,000. The low-income senior freeze must be renewed every year. (source: https://wincoil.gov/departments/supervisor-of-assessments/exemption-forms-information)

recorder.address: 115 N Main Street, Room 202, Eureka, IL 61530

notes: The Woodford County Circuit Clerk's office is on the 2nd floor of the courthouse, which has an e-filing kiosk there and a law library on the 3rd floor. Courthouse hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (source: https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/courts-directory/58/Woodford-County-Courthouse/court/)

The Woodford County Clerk and Recorder is at 115 N Main Street, Room 202, phone 309-467-2822. The office records, indexes and scans documents qualified to be recorded by statute, including deeds, and holds records since the late 1830s. (source: https://woodford-county.org/157)
